provenance.label: numerical solution of the stated model; not experimental validation
provenance.solver: STRATO BTCS five-layer spherical finite difference

markers: every release record is a set of discrete markers: bound markers (black downward triangles) at the bound value with no deviation and no status word; point markers only where a point comparison exists; no experimental line is drawn

observations.particle_applicability: compact with intact particles only; not matrix-corrected; mean particle release plus matrix and background contribution
observations.premise_source: digitised total read as an upper bound
observations.systematic_uncertainty: 5 % gamma counting (Stempien 2023 p. 10), kept separate and not combined into any number on a graph
premises: The reported total contains all material released by the compact during the test (no loss to uncounted surfaces; open point O13).

The kernel-only start (decision 20) differs from the real initial state in two ways with opposite effects: it ignores the inventory already outside the SiC (raises F_p) and the inventory already in the coatings (lowers F_p). The size of the difference is not stated here: the results pipeline computes it for Sr-90 and Cs-137 from the Scenario 5 heating runs against the kernel-only runs of the same histories and writes it into the files curves/s5.refuelling.heating*.json, field kernel_only_comparison. The net direction is not established for Ag-110m and Cs-134.

A1: the model fraction is a fraction of one intact particle's inventory; a compact total that is not matrix-corrected includes inventory that was already outside the SiC, so it is at most an upper bound.
